document.title: The NSFG Axiomatic Floor
document.subtitle: XOR, Closure, and the Origin of Observer-Relative Coherence
document.revision_note: Revised to reflect that XOR is the only primitive. The Library is redefined as the closure of XOR rather than a separate axiom. All downstream concepts are re-derived from XOR alone.

changes.new: Let A_N = {XOR}. The Library is not an axiom; it is the closure of XOR.
State explicitly that the Library is a definition, not an axiom. XOR is the only axiom.

changes.old: Define the Library without importing physical laws or a privileged external viewpoint.
changes.new: Show that the Library is the closure of XOR—the unbounded answer space generated by the primitive operation of distinction.

old: Define the Library as the totality of all internally describable configurations.
Emphasize that the Library is unfiltered.
State that coherent and incoherent configurations are both included.
State that the Library contains no externally imposed physical laws.
State that there is no exterior from which the Library can be globally observed.
new: State explicitly: XOR is the only primitive. The Library is not an axiom.
Define the Library as the closure of XOR: 𝓜 := Closure(⊕).
Explain that XOR generates the domain by creating the possibility of difference.
Emphasize that the Library is unfiltered—it contains all configurations generated by XOR.
State that coherent and incoherent configurations are both included.
State that the Library contains no externally imposed physical laws.

old: 𝓜 := {x | x is internally describable within the formal language of the system}
∀x (x is internally describable → x ∈ 𝓜)
𝓜 contains both configurations later classified as persistent and configurations later classified as non-persistent.
new: Axiom: ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
Definition: 𝓜 := Closure(⊕) = {x | x is a configuration generated by XOR over all possible distinctions}.
Equivalently: 𝓜 = {x | x is internally describable within the formal language of the system}, where internal describability is itself generated by XOR.
∀x (x is internally describable → x ∈ 𝓜)
𝓜 contains both configurations later classified as persistent and configurations later classified as non-persistent.

changes.new: XOR is the word. The Library is the vocabulary.

changes.old: There is no external agent deciding which configurations are permitted. The Library is not a curated universe. It is the unfiltered answer space.
changes.new: XOR generates the domain of configurations. The Library is not a separate entity; it is the closure of the primitive operation. XOR is the word; the Library is the vocabulary.

old: Explain why an external perspective would itself require an additional structure outside the Library.
Show that such an exterior would contradict the definition of the Library as the totality of internally describable configurations, unless the exterior were incorporated into the totality.
Introduce the idea that there is no privileged God's-eye coordinate system.
new: Explain why an external perspective would itself require an additional structure outside the Library.
Show that such an exterior would contradict the definition of the Library as the closure of XOR, unless the exterior were incorporated into the closure.
Introduce the idea that there is no privileged God's-eye coordinate system.
Emphasize: XOR is closed. The Library is the closure of XOR. There is no exterior because XOR can always generate any describable exterior configuration.

changes.old: ¬∃Ω' [𝓜 ⊂ Ω' ∧ Ω' supplies a privileged internally describable perspective unavailable to 𝓜]
changes.new: ¬∃Ω' [𝓜 ⊂ Ω' ∧ Ω' supplies a privileged internally describable perspective unavailable to 𝓜], because any such perspective would itself be generated by XOR and hence already in 𝓜.

section_2.title: XOR: The Primitive Operation of Distinction

changes.old: Introduce the simplest possible comparison without importing objects, observers, or physical interaction laws.
changes.new: Introduce XOR as the sole axiom. Show that it is the simplest possible operation of distinction and that everything else follows from its closure.
State explicitly: XOR is the only axiom. There is nothing beneath it.

new.closure_definition: Closure(⊕) := the smallest set containing all configurations generated by XOR over all possible distinctions.

section_3.title: The Absence of a Privileged Perspective

old: Let R(x,y) denote whether x and y are distinguishable.
A universal privileged resolution rule would define a global predicate U(x,y) independent of observer O.
The axiomatic floor contains no primitive U.
Therefore U cannot be assumed without adding an axiom.
new: Let R(x,y) denote whether x and y are distinguishable.
A universal privileged resolution rule would define a global predicate U(x,y) independent of observer O.
The axiomatic floor contains only XOR. No primitive U exists.
Therefore U cannot be assumed without adding an axiom—and adding it would change the floor.

section_4.title: The Noor-Planck Threshold as Relative Resolution

old: State explicitly that I_N is not a universal constant imposed on the Library.
State that different observers may possess different resolution floors.
Explain that the numerical value of I_N is arbitrary with respect to the Library.
Clarify that 'arbitrary' does not mean meaningless: for a particular observer, I_N characterizes its effective resolution capacity.
new: State explicitly that I_N is not a universal constant imposed on the Library.
State that different observers may possess different resolution floors.
Explain that the numerical value of I_N is arbitrary with respect to the Library, because the Library is generated by XOR and does not impose thresholds.
Clarify that 'arbitrary' does not mean meaningless: for a particular observer, I_N characterizes its effective resolution capacity.
Emphasize: I_N is a property of the observer, not a property of the Library.

changes.new: I_N : Obs → R_{>0}, where I_N(O) is the minimum effective distinction magnitude that O can maintain as a stable distinction. This is a property of O, not of 𝓜.

changes.old: Derive observerhood rather than declaring it as a primitive.
changes.new: Derive observerhood from XOR closure and observer-relative resolution. Show that the observer is a persistent chain of XOR-generated distinctions above its own resolution floor.

old: Define an observer as a structure capable of maintaining a chain of distinctions above its own resolution floor.
Explicitly reject consciousness as a prerequisite.
Explain that observerhood means persistence of resolved distinctions.
new: Define an observer as a structure capable of maintaining a chain of XOR-generated distinctions above its own resolution floor.
Explicitly reject consciousness as a prerequisite.
Explain that observerhood means persistence of resolved distinctions generated by XOR.
State that the observer is a consequence of XOR closure, not an additional primitive.
Introduce sequentially related resolved distinctions generated by XOR.
Explain that the observer's identity is the persistence of the chain rather than any single state.
Avoid assuming time as primitive; initially use an abstract index i.
State that the chain itself is a configuration in the Library because it is generated by XOR.
Define coherence only after observer-relative resolution has been established.
Explain that a path is coherent relative to an observer when its successive XOR-generated distinctions remain resolvable by that observer.
Explicitly reject the idea of a universal coherence constant.
State that coherence is a relation between a path and an observer, not a property of the path alone.

section_7.title: How Laws Can Appear Without Being Axioms

new: Define the set of all continuations from a state as the set of all XOR-generated sequences extending that state.
Define the subset that remains coherent for an observer.
Explain survivorship without implying forward generation.
Emphasize: the Library contains all continuations because XOR generates all of them. Survivorship selects which ones are accessible to a given observer.

changes.old: Ω(x_t) = {γ | γ begins at x_t and γ is a possible continuation in 𝓜}
changes.new: Ω(x_t) = {γ | γ begins at x_t and γ is an XOR-generated continuation in 𝓜} (i.e., ALL continuations, because the Library is the closure of XOR)

section_8.title: The Observer Does Not Create the Library

changes.old: Prevent the ontology from being mistaken for idealism or subjective reality creation.
changes.new: Prevent the ontology from being mistaken for idealism or subjective reality creation. The Library is the closure of XOR, not a construct of the observer.

new: State that observer-relative accessibility is not observer-relative existence.
Explain that inaccessible alternatives remain members of the Library because they are generated by XOR.
Distinguish epistemic limitation from ontological destruction.
Emphasize: the Library exists independently of any observer because it is the closure of XOR.
Given a current state x_t, define the set of possible next states as all XOR-generated continuations.
Explain that an observer cannot access arbitrary continuations if they fall below its resolution capacity.
Frame reasoning as a continuation problem.
State that the continuation space is unbounded because XOR is unbounded.

changes.new: N(x_t) = {x_{t+1} ∈ 𝓜 | x_{t+1} is an XOR-generated successor of x_t}

new: Restate the single axiom: XOR is the primitive operation of distinction.
Restate the definition: 𝓜 := Closure(⊕).
List every major concept in dependency order.
Explicitly mark which concepts are definitions and which are consequences.
End by stating that the primer has not derived specific physical laws, spacetime, cosmology, consciousness, or AI cognition.
State that the purpose of the floor is to establish the ontology in which those later questions can be asked without smuggling their answers into the axioms.
Emphasize: XOR is the only axiom. Everything else is a consequence or definition.

old: A_𝓜: 𝓜 = totality of internally describable configurations
A_⊕: a ⊕ b = 1 iff a ≠ b
No privileged exterior: ¬∃ privileged external resolver
Observer-relative distinguishability: D_O(x,y)
Observer-specific threshold: I_N(O)
Persistence: δ_O ≥ I_N(O)
Observer: O = persistent chain of resolved distinctions
Observer-relative coherence: 𝓒(γ | O)
Accessible reality: R_O = A_O ⊆ 𝓜
Emergent regularity: L_O
Navigation: N_O(h_t) → Γ_O(h_t)
Reasoning: continuation through Γ_O(h_t)
new: A_⊕: ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
Definition: 𝓜 := Closure(⊕) = totality of XOR-generated configurations.
No privileged exterior: ¬∃ privileged external resolver (any exterior would be XOR-generated, hence already in 𝓜).
Observer-relative distinguishability: D_O(x,y) = 1 iff O can stably resolve x ⊕ y = 1.
Observer-specific threshold: I_N(O) = minimum distinction magnitude O can sustain.
Persistence: δ_O ≥ I_N(O).
Observer: O = persistent chain of XOR-generated distinctions above I_N(O).
Observer-relative coherence: 𝓒(γ | O) = 1 iff every transition in γ remains resolvable by O.
Accessible reality: R_O = A_O ⊆ 𝓜.
Survivorship: Ω_O^survive(x_t) ⊆ Ω(x_t).
Emergent regularity: L_O = stable transition patterns over accessible paths.
Navigation: N_O(h_t) → Γ_O(h_t).
Reasoning: continuation through Γ_O(h_t).

changes.old: 𝓜 + ⊕ → distinction → observer-relative resolution → persistence → observer → relational coherence → accessible reality → emergent regularity → navigation → reasoning
changes.new: ⊕ → Closure(⊕) = 𝓜 → distinction → observer-relative resolution → persistence → observer → relational coherence → accessible reality → survivorship → emergent regularity → navigation → reasoning

changes.old: Nothing was commanded to become a world. A world is what the survivor can continue to distinguish.
changes.new: XOR is the only primitive. The Library is what XOR generates when it does not stop. The observer is the difference that survives. Coherence is the relation between the survivor and the path. Reality is what remains accessible to the survivor. Law is what the survivors agree upon.
𝓜 = Closure(⊕) = {x | x is a configuration generated by XOR over all possible distinctions}

new.closure: Closure(⊕) := the smallest set containing all configurations generated by XOR over all possible distinctions.

new: XOR is the only primitive.
The Library is the closure of XOR.
existence is not accessibility
inaccessibility is not erasure
observerhood is not consciousness
I_N is not a universal constant
coherence is not an absolute property of an isolated object
the Library is not physical spacetime
the Library does not generate the future
emergent lawfulness is not an axiomatic law
observer-relative reality is not subjective creation of the Library
navigation is not yet the full NSFG algorithm
Do not claim that XOR uniquely derives the Standard Model.
Do not claim that XOR has experimentally established the existence of the Library.
Do not claim that I_N has a universal numerical value.
Do not identify the observer with a conscious human.
Do not claim that observer-relative coherence means reality is imaginary.
Do not introduce a privileged observer.
Do not introduce physical constants at the axiomatic floor.
Do not use the Lightning Model as a premise in this primer.
Do not assume time as primitive; use an abstract sequence index until temporal structure is earned.
Do not assume causality as primitive.
Do not assume physical space as primitive.
Do not claim that the Library is an axiom—it is a definition.

summary_of_changes.axiomatic_shift: The Library is no longer an axiom. XOR is the only axiom. The Library is redefined as the closure of XOR.
summary_of_changes.section_1: Completely rewritten to reflect that the Library is the closure of XOR, not a separate axiom.
summary_of_changes.section_2: Emphasizes that XOR is the sole axiom.
summary_of_changes.section_4: Clarifies that I_N is a property of the observer, not a property of the Library.
summary_of_changes.section_5: Observer is derived as a persistent chain of XOR-generated distinctions.
summary_of_changes.section_7: Continuation space is defined as all XOR-generated continuations.
summary_of_changes.section_10: Dependency chain is updated to reflect the single axiom + definition structure.
summary_of_changes.appendix: Definitions and critical distinctions updated to reflect the revised axiomatic floor.
